families.title: Bayesian and Markov networks
families.intro: Networks against the tools people use for them: Ace 3.0, which compiles a network into an arithmetic circuit, and Merlin 1.7.0's bucket-tree elimination (`-a bte`, and `-t PR` for the partition function), and the other exact network tools: pyAgrum (junction tree), pgmpy (variable elimination), libDAI (junction tree) and TensorInference.jl (tensor network contraction; of its two contraction orders, `treesa` and `greedy`, the faster is shown). On the standard suite's networks, Ace's networks, the large networks and the UAI networks ProbLog, PITA and aspmc ran too. The exact systems that read Dice programs, Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Geni and Pluck, ran on the standard suite's networks, Ace's networks, the large networks and the UAI networks, each network as the Dice program of [`scripts/gen_bn.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/gen_bn.py). tddlog reads a network as a ProbLog program, one annotated disjunction per row of a table.

setup: Five jobs on four lab machines (36 physical cores and 503 GB; 20 physical cores and 503 GB; 16 physical cores and 251 GB; 16 physical cores and 125 GB), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-21: every baseline of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes; Ace in 12 wide lanes of 88 GB, half of it its Java heap, and tddlog alone in a later job for each, on the same machine, in the same lanes, with the same limits and repetitions (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-28) but the UAI networks's in 32 lanes rather than 8, with the same 31 GB a process, the UAI networks asked P(e)'s in 28 lanes rather than 14, with the same 35 GB a process, std's in 10 lanes rather than 34, with 25 GB a process and the final PR set's in 17 lanes rather than 34, with the same 29 GB a process. Each comparison pairs a baseline with tddlog run on the same machine in the same lanes.

Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced. Alea.jl's and Roulette's own times leave out the start-up and compilation of Julia and Racket, as on the page of the Dice family's suites; their processes' wall times are columns of their own.

tddlog 0.1.0 with its default strategy (`auto`), linked statically as of 2026-10-26 (tididi 968e17f0, goatd e592d1e). Ace 3.0, Merlin 1.7.0, pyAgrum 3.2.1, pgmpy 1.1.2, libDAI 0.3.2, TensorInference.jl, ProbLog 2.3.0, PITA (cplint) and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD. Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Geni and Pluck as on the page of the Dice family's suites.

Every answer of tddlog's, and of each other system, is compared with a reference: the clique tree ([`scripts/bn_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/bn_exact.py)), Ace or Merlin. The largest absolute differences: 1.9e-14 on Ace's networks, 4.9e-11 on the large networks, 9.1e-14 on the 111 UAI networks the clique tree answers (the other five agree with Merlin's six printed digits); no other system answers Grids_15, Grids_16, Grids_17 and Grids_18. For the partition function tddlog's log10 Z agrees with every other exact answer there is: Merlin's, the clique tree's, or a weighted model count of the network. The other network tools' answers against the same references: pyAgrum 249 marginal runs to 3.6e-7 and 235 partition functions to 2.1e-7 in log10; pgmpy 159 marginal runs to 3.6e-7 and 214 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10; libDAI 257 marginal runs to 5.0e-7 and 262 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10; TensorInference.jl 391 marginal runs to 5.0e-7 and 394 partition functions to 2.2e-7 in log10 (the tools print six digits, as Merlin does). A baseline's answer off the reference by more than 1e-9 and either by more than 1e-6 or by more than 1e-3 of it, beyond the last digit either of the two prints, counts as a failure (wrong).

suites.title: Literature suite
suites.about: 98 programs of ten families from published evaluations: mnist_sum, pedigree, sickness, noisy-or, mastermind and pdb, each grown on a random structure from a seed, Prob-EC's event calculus over T frames (eventcalc), PSouffle's taint analyses of 15 Android apps (taint), Beame et al.'s safe queries QW and Q9 on a complete domain (liftsep) and paths of two edges in random graphs (rgraph); 300 s a run. ProvSQL ran on the four tuple-independent families, pdb, noisy-or, liftsep and rgraph (the others are recursive or have annotated disjunctions).

suites.title: TPC-H
suites.about: The TPC-H queries as Boolean queries over a tuple-independent database, at scale factors 0.001 to 1, flat and through views (295 instances); 600 s a run.

suites.title: Biomine
suites.about: The probability that each of four genes is connected to Alzheimer disease in the human Biomine network, over the union of the K most probable paths, for ten values of K up to 64; 600 s a run.

setup: Three jobs on two lab machines (36 and 20 physical cores, 503 GB each), 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-20: every baseline of a suite in the same job, each run single-threaded and pinned to a physical core of its own, side by side in lanes; Ace in 12 wide lanes of 88 GB, half of it its Java heap, and tddlog alone in a later job for each, on the same machine, in the same lanes, with the same limits and repetitions (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-28) but the UAI networks's in 32 lanes rather than 8, with the same 31 GB a process, the UAI networks asked P(e)'s in 28 lanes rather than 14, with the same 35 GB a process, std's in 10 lanes rather than 34, with 25 GB a process and the final PR set's in 17 lanes rather than 34, with the same 29 GB a process. Each comparison pairs a baseline with tddlog run on the same machine in the same lanes.

Wall time of the whole process, parsing and grounding included. A system's fastest variant is the one shown: ProbLog's d-DNNF, SDD or forward SDD compilation; Ace's default route or c2d forced. Alea.jl's and Roulette's own times leave out the start-up and compilation of Julia and Racket, as on the page of the Dice family's suites; their processes' wall times are columns of their own.

tddlog 0.1.0 with its default strategy (`auto`), linked statically as of 2026-10-22 (tididi c7c0c5d6, goatd e592d1e). The event-calculus programs, the reruns of the literature scan's taint apps and the growth sizes ran a build of 2026-10-25 with twin contraction (tididi b9e5064e, goatd e592d1e) and a recursion over a successor relation grounded level by level, which lacks only the release's sparse route (tididi 9fc0a599). The runs on Bayesian and Markov networks ran a build of 2026-10-26 that reads Bayesian and Markov network files itself (tididi 968e17f0, goatd e592d1e). The runs on Dice programs and LPADs ran a build of 2026-10-27 that reads Dice programs and LPADs itself (tididi 7eb08230, goatd e592d1e). Beside a cross job's systems, one run of tddlog on an instance where the rerun's was skipped ran that job's build, as of 2026-10-20 (tididi c7c0c5d6, goatd e592d1e). The release's main contains every solver change those builds have. ProbLog 2.3.0, PITA (cplint) and aspmc with sharpSAT-TD; ProvSQL 1.13.0 on PostgreSQL 16.4. Ace 3.0, Merlin 1.7.0, pyAgrum 3.2.1, pgmpy 1.1.2, libDAI 0.3.2 and TensorInference.jl. Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Geni and Pluck as on the page of the Dice family's suites.

Every answer of tddlog's is compared with a reference: ProbLog's, or an exact solver written for the suite ([`scripts/lit_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/lit_exact.py), [`scripts/tpch_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/tpch_exact.py), [`scripts/reliability_exact.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/reliability_exact.py)). The largest absolute differences: 3.6e-7 on the standard suite (ProbLog prints eight digits), 5.0e-9 on the literature suite, 4.0e-14 on TPC-H, 3.4e-12 on Biomine; ProvSQL's answers differ from the reference's by at most 5.3e-12 on TPC-H and by at most 8.9e-16 on pdb and noisy-or. The random graphs and grids no exact system finishes agree with estimates from sampled graphs ([`scripts/sample_paths.py`](https://github.com/Tractables/tddlog/blob/baselines/scripts/sample_paths.py)). A baseline's answer off the reference by more than 1e-9 and either by more than 1e-6 or by more than 1e-3 of it, beyond the last digit either of the two prints, counts as a failure (wrong).
